title: Geopolitics and shipping disruption are the biggest risks for 2027
gist: Oxford Economics' UAE roundtable finds geopolitical escalation and shipping disruption the top 2027 risks, with oil seen falling to $80-100 by end-2027 and clients upbeat on AI investment but worried about job displacement.

insights.claim: 71% of UAE roundtable participants view geopolitical escalation as the most pressing global issue, with regional conflicts shaping their outlook.
insights.so_what: Client sentiment in the Gulf is dominated by conflict risk.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane

insights.claim: Attacks on shipping facilities, sluggish tourism recovery and the possibility of a real estate bubble bursting were flagged as critical risks to the UAE economy into 2027.
insights.so_what: Watch UAE property and tourism-linked assets for conflict sensitivity.
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane

insights.claim: Oil prices are expected to fall to between $80 and $100 per barrel by the end of 2027.
insights.so_what: A still-elevated oil path supports Gulf fiscal positions but implies a decline from current levels.
insights.locator: While oil prices are expected to fall
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane

insights.claim: Clients remain optimistic that AI investments will contribute positively to GDP growth, though they worry about job displacement from AI and its effect on local demand.
insights.so_what: Gulf AI investment is a growth narrative with a consumption risk.
insights.locator: While oil prices are expected to fall
insights.speaker: Sanele Mjikane
